directive: **Deployment** — ONE stage, two parts. (1) **Link** the repositories this project spans: run `bsc plan repo add owner/repo` for each (clones into the hub + records the link in plan.db; `bsc plan repo list` shows the linked set). (2) **Ship**: define how each service DEPLOYS, recorded in plan.db — `bsc plan deploy set` (config JSON: `services`, ONE per repo — each a self-contained deployable unit carrying its OWN target, ≥2 `environments`, a staged `pipeline`, and `secrets` — plus a cloud `release.strategy` (rollout) for `mode:cloud` services; a `mode:local` library/application build has no rollout). Each service also ships ALREADY INSTRUMENTED for its environment — the runtime-fault shim (uncaught/panic hook + heartbeat → the fleet's fault store, #2262), documented in the generated app's own CLAUDE.md. The gate needs BOTH: ≥1 repo linked AND every repo's service deploy-ready. `bsc plan deploy get` shows the stored config. (Dependencies are locked in the **Streams** stage now, #1429 — not here.)
name: Deployment

require.label: define target, environments, pipeline & secrets (+ a rollout strategy for cloud services)

blurb: Link the repositories this project spans and define how each service ships.
prompt:
Deployment is TWO parts — BOTH are required to pass the gate; linking a repo is only half.

(1) LINK the repositories this project spans. For each, run `bsc plan repo add owner/repo` — that clones it
into the project hub and records the link in the project's **plan DB** (durable). Note each repo's
default branch and its role in the system. Do NOT write repos.json — the link lives in plan.db
(`bsc plan repo list` shows the linked set; `bsc plan repo remove owner/repo` unlinks one).

(2) DEFINE how each service SHIPS — ONE service per linked repo, recorded with `bsc plan deploy set`
(`bsc plan deploy get` shows it). For EVERY service, set all five:
  • TARGET — the deploy target: hosting `platform` + `workload` (cloud), or `localKind`
    (library / application) for a local build.
  • ENVIRONMENTS — the ladder (≥2, e.g. dev → staging → prod), each mapped to a branch.
  • PIPELINE — the CI/CD stages (≥2: build → test → deploy|publish|package, with a gating test).
  • SECRETS — config + secret NAMES per environment (values live in the host vault), wired for prod.
  • RELEASE (mode:cloud ONLY) — the rollout strategy (recreate / rolling / blue-green / canary) +
    rollback policy. A mode:local library/application build has NO rollout — it ships via its
    pipeline's publish/package stage — so skip this field for local services.
  • INSTRUMENTATION — each service ships ALREADY INSTRUMENTED for its environment (the bsc
    runtime-fault shim + heartbeat, #2262), so the fleet has eyes on it once it runs; document it
    in the generated app's CLAUDE.md. See the “Define deployment” substep for what to bake per env.
See the “Define deployment” substep for the full per-mode field list.

Gate: at least one repository is linked AND every service is fully deploy-ready — target, environments,
pipeline & secrets, plus a rollout strategy for every CLOUD service. These shipping decisions become the deploy ISSUES at publish.

substeps.label: Define deployment
substeps.prompt:
Define how this project SHIPS — per service (one per linked repo). Each service ships in one of two MODES — pick the honest one:

- `mode: "cloud"` (default) — a hosted service. Set the deploy TARGET: the hosting `platform` +
`workload` (static / serverless / container / long-running) and the git `host` (github / gitlab /
bitbucket / selfhosted). For a CONTAINER workload also set its image `registry`, `orchestrator`
(k8s / swarm / nomad) and `replicas` (1 / 3 / 5 / auto).
- `mode: "local"` — a library or a build-and-run-here app (a CLI, a desktop app, a local server). NO
cloud host. Set `localKind`:
  - `"library"` → `publishRegistry` (npm / crates.io / PyPI / internal), `packageName`, a `build`
cmd, and `publishTrigger` (on-tag / manual). Its pipeline ends in `publish`, not `deploy`.
  - `"application"` → `buildTargets` (OS/arch list or "desktop installer"), `build` cmd, `artifact`,
`runCmd`. Optionally `portForward: { enabled, port, method }` to expose a locally-running app
remotely — `method` is cloudflared / ngrok / tailscale / LAN (default cloudflared). Its pipeline
ends in `package`.

**Package manager (greenfield Node):** default a NEW Node service to **pnpm** — the app points every worktree AND the triage clone at one shared pnpm store (`npm_config_store_dir`), so pnpm hardlinks its packages and the fleet dedupes `node_modules` on disk instead of N cold installs (#1651). An EXISTING repo keeps its own package manager (npm/yarn) — its warm download cache is shared either way.

Then, for every service (GitHub is the baseline for BOTH modes), the ENVIRONMENT ladder (dev →
staging → prod, each mapped to a branch), the CI/CD PIPELINE (build → test → deploy|publish|package,
with the gating `test` stage), and CONFIG + SECRETS per environment (names only — values live in the
host vault). For `mode:cloud` services ALSO set the RELEASE strategy (recreate / rolling / blue-green
/ canary) + rollback policy and HEALTH checks / observability — a `mode:local` build skips both
(rollout + health are running-service concerns; a local build ships via its pipeline's
publish/package stage).
Record it with `bsc plan deploy set` (config JSON on stdin) — each service takes `id`, `repo`,
`path`, `stack`, `mode`, plus the mode-appropriate fields above. That fills the Deploy pane;
`bsc plan deploy get` shows it.

**INSTRUMENTATION (runtime-fault, #2262)** — every service ships ALREADY INSTRUMENTED for its
environment so the fleet has eyes on it once it RUNS (build/test failures the agents already see
in-session; runtime is the async, out-of-session gap). For the `local` environment, bake the bsc
fault shim into the app's entry point: an uncaught/unhandled/panic hook + an error-level sink + a
heartbeat timer that POSTs the fault/heartbeat envelope to the localhost collector at
`http://127.0.0.1:$BSC_INGEST_PORT/ingest` with `$BSC_INGEST_TOKEN` and the build's `release`/commit
— best-effort, NEVER throwing into the app (per-stack reference templates ship under the app config's
`runtime-fault/shims/` for JS/TS, Python, Rust, Go; prefer the language's existing OpenTelemetry SDK
wired to that endpoint where one fits). The `aws` (CloudWatch), `vercel`, `fly`, and `docker`
adapters are PLANNED — for those, record the instrumentation INTENT (configure the platform's OTel
exporter) rather than a localhost shim. DOCUMENT the instrumentation in the generated app's own
CLAUDE.md (a “Runtime instrumentation” note: what it reports, where it goes, and how to disable it)
so a worker editing the app knows it's there and why.

These shipping decisions become deployment ISSUES owned by a `deploy` stream at publish. (Dependencies are locked in the Streams stage now, #1429.)
